method: exact integer scan of canonical greedy Zeckendorf digits
identity_used: phi^j = F_(j-1) + F_j phi and norm(a + b phi) = a^2 + ab - b^2
command: ruby -rjson -e 'f=[0,1];30.times{f<<f[-1]+f[-2]}; zeck=->(n){digits=[]; i=f.length-1; while n>0; i-=1 while f[i]>n; digits<<i; n-=f[i]; i-=1; end; digits}; violations=[]; zero_norms=[]; samples=[]; (1..100000).each{|v| digits=zeck.call(v); a=digits.sum{|j|f[j-1]}; b=digits.sum{|j|f[j]}; q=a*a+a*b-b*b; violations<<{v:v,digits:digits,norm:q} unless (digits.min.even? ? q>0 : q<0); zero_norms<<{v:v,digits:digits} if q==0; samples<<[v,digits,digits.min%2,q] if v<=12}; puts JSON.generate({tested:100000,sign_violations:violations.length,zero_norms:zero_norms.length,first_violation:violations.first,samples:samples})'

nearby_false_variant.claim: the greatest occupied Zeckendorf index determines the norm sign

falsifier: Any positive v whose least occupied Zeckendorf index has even parity and nonpositive norm, odd parity and nonnegative norm, or zero norm.
interpretation: The scan supplies finite exact evidence for the open statement. It is not a Lean proof and does not establish the universal claim.
